scope: Proposition 5.5 (Endpoint potentials) of the manuscript “Cardy’s formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation” (preprints/Cardys-formula-for-critical-Poisson-Voronoi-percolation-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 224 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1334302b31272ae0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every admitted departure or arrival placement and type there are centered state functions ϕX,+ s and ϕX,− t , allowed to depend on ε, with ∥ϕX,+ s ∥L2(µs) ≤ Cshorth, ∥ϕX,− t ∥L2(µt) ≤ Cshorth. They depend only on the indicated endpoint data, and not on the long connector or its allowed small chart changes. For each fixed connector e : s → t of class size k, provided |zt − zs| > Ch(1 + k), iε e(σs, σt) = aX h (zt − zs) + ϕX,+ s (σs) + ϕX,− t (σt) + bε e + ρε e, ∥ρε e∥L1(µs⊗µt) −→ 0, lim sup ε→0 |bε e| ≤ Cshorth(1 + k). (5.3) Here bε e is deterministic. The constants depend on the fixed normalized menu and short templates, but not on a thin fitted connector, its length or a finite cover of such connectors.
